title: Network corridor reference + Terraform sprint lab (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a compact, reusable reference architecture we call the \"network corridor\" and a hands-on Terraform sprint lab for customer VPC onboarding and controlled upgrades. The idea is to provide an operationally lightweight, repeatable pattern for connecting customer VPCs (cloud or on-prem) to Redwood Private deployments with clear preflight checks, TF module layout, acceptance tests, and rollback guidance.

Audience:
- Solutions engineers executing VPC onboarding and field engineers running pre-production handoffs.
- Platform/infra engineers who will maintain the TF modules and CI checks.
- SREs and customer success for upgrade coordination.

High-level pattern overview (network corridor):
- Transit corridor: a narrow set of routable prefixes and an egress/ingress transit path (transit VPC or on-prem router) that carries only Redwood inference traffic.
- Segmented subnets for control plane, inference data path, and optional edge-proxy.
- Egress policy layer: per-tenant NAT/proxy for audit and filtering (optionally using a proxy sidecar or managed gateway).
- Service connectivity: mTLS/Mutual-auth connection between customer-side proxy and Redwood edge with explicit allowed CIDR ranges and port restrictions.
- Optional airgap: pre-baked ETL cassette (s3-like appliance) + scheduled sync jobs when customer forbids direct egress.

Why this name?
Network corridor intentionally narrows blast radius and simplifies ACLs: single transit path + small prefix set -> easier monitoring, simpler TF modules, deterministic failure modes.

Quick checklist (pre-kickoff):
- Customer has a POC account + admin contact and network owner identified.
- Customer confirms CIDR plan and whether NAT/egress is required.
- Required ports/protocols: TCP 443 outbound to Redwood control plane, TCP 5222 (if agent heartbeats used), and ephemeral TCP for model streaming.
- KMS/HSM integration required? (yes/no)
- Compliance constraints: data residency/airgap/egress auditing
- Identify contact IP ranges for destination (Redwood egress IPs) and gather SLA windows for maintenance.

Terraform sprint lab: modules and layout (recommendation)
- repo/layout: terraform-modules/
  - modules/transit-vpc/  (creates transit network, gateways, route tables)
  - modules/tenant-attachment/ (sets up routes, security groups, peering/attachments)
  - modules/egress-proxy/ (optional, deploys proxy VM or k8s manifest + nat)
  - modules/kms-hooks/ (KMS keys + grants; no plaintext secrets in state)
  - envs/customer-<short>/  (root module referencing above)
Key module contract notes (interface):
- modules/transit-vpc input: allowed_prefixes (list), region, extra_tags
- modules/tenant-attachment input: tenant_id, attachment_type (vpc-peering/vpn/transit-gw), customer_routes (map)
- modules/egress-proxy output: proxy_ips (list), proxy_cidrs
- modules/kms-hooks: accepts a list of GRANT_PRINCIPAL_ARNs (string list)

Design constraints and TF best-practices:
- Keep module state narrow: per-tenant state files (workspaces or separate state backends) to allow independent rollbacks.
- Use explicit lifecycle.ignore_changes for fields changed by network admins (e.g., route table associations that might be mutated by customer automation).
- Avoid implicit dependencies on shared resources; pass IDs explicitly to modules.
- Enforce tagging and owner metadata on all resources (owner, project, ticket id).

Sample (pseudo) variables.tf snippet to include in the tenant root module:
- variable \"tenant_id\" { type = string }
- variable \"customer_cidr\" { type = list(string) }
- variable \"egress_required\" { type = bool, default = true }
- locals { corridor_prefixes = [for p in var.customer_cidr : cidrsubnet(p, 8, 0)] }

Acceptance tests (post-provision):
1) Control plane connectivity: attempt to POST /v1/health to Redwood control plane endpoint from a bastion inside tenant corridor. Expect 200 and TLS CN validation.
2) Token flow: Ensure customer-managed KMS grants allow Redwood service principal to wrap/unwrap keys; run a wrap/unwrap test artifact.
3) Stream test: open a 5s streaming generation session and validate no packet drops >0.5% and latency under agreed SLO (e.g. p95 < 150ms).
4) ACL verification: run port scans (internal only) against corridor proxies to confirm only allowed ports are reachable.

Upgrade plan (minor network-only change):
- Phase 0 (preflight): run tf plan with --target for changed modules in isolated workspace; produce plan artifact + diff.
- Phase 1 (canary tenant): apply to a single non-prod tenant with telemetry enabled for 24h.
- Phase 2 (staged rollout): expand to a 10% tenant cohort timed in service window. Monitor packet drops, auth errors, and control-plane heartbeats.
- Phase 3 (ramp to all): full apply with a rolling window and automated alert thresholds.
- Rollback: re-apply previous state snapshot; if state-level rollback is not trivial, tear down newly added routes/gateways first.

Preflight checks (scriptable):
- terraform validate && tflint
- aws-vpc-checker --cidr-conflicts
- kms-policy-lint against expected grants
- smoke-run: curl from test-bastion to control-plane

Operator runbook snippets (cheat-sheet):
- To plan for tenant alpha: cd envs/customer-alpha && TF_VAR_tenant_id=alpha terraform plan -out alpha.plan
- To apply just transit changes: terraform apply -target=module.transit-vpc
- To snapshot state before change: terraform state pull > state-<tenant>-YYYYMMDD.json
- To rollback quickly: terraform apply -refresh=false previous-plan.binary (if you saved the plan)

Failure modes and mitigations:
- Route leak to customer default internet: mitigation = remove propagated routes and restrict route table association; immediately add blackhole route for stray prefixes.
- Proxy CPU exhaustion: autoscale or failover to managed egress OR add rate-limiting on device to reduce burst traffic.
- KMS grants mismatch: emergency path = rotate a short-lived key, update grant, and re-run wrap/unwrap smoke test. Keep documented contact for KMS admin.

Security and compliance notes:
- Do not store plaintext API keys in TF. Use remote state with encryption and state-locking.
- Require audit logging (VPC flow logs) for corridor subnets for at least 30 days for high-risk tenants.
- For airgapped tenants, prefer signed package deliveries and an approval manifest with checksum.

Lab scenario (30-90 minute exercise):
- Objective: onboard a mock tenant with a transit corridor behind a transit-gw + attach a small egress proxy.
- Steps:
  1) Checkout repo, create a workspace envs/customer-mock
  2) Fill variables: tenant_id=mock, customer_cidr=[10.70.0.0/16]
  3) Run terraform init && terraform plan -> validate outputs: proxy_ips and corridor_prefixes
  4) Apply with --auto-approve and confirm outputs
  5) From bastion (provided in lab) run curl health + streaming test
  6) Intentionally add a bad route (simulate customer mistake) and run detection script to verify alert triggers

Observability/telemetry checklist (must-haves before handoff):
- VPC flow logs enabled and shipped to our observability pipeline with tags for tenant_id
- SSH bastion access logs configured and mapped to ticket owner
- Proxy metrics: conn_count, cpu, latency p50/p95
- SLI dashboard with p95 latency, success rate, and egress bytes per tenant

Open questions / known TODOs (for sprint):
- Define exact port list for model streaming (placeholder in this doc) and validate with runtime team (Samir owns).
- Decide on whether to bake a lightweight layer 7 proxy image we manage vs using customer-managed proxies. Tradeoff: version control vs operational footprint.
- Add pre-commit hooks and automated linting to TF repo for tag enforcement.

Concluding notes:
This draft is intended to be practical — keep modules opinionated but small, make tenant state independently rollbackable, and enforce corridor isolation to speed up troubleshooting during onboarding or upgrades. Use the lab as a verification gate before any customer rollout.

Appendix: quick tf plan checklist (for engineers)
- Run terraform fmt && terraform validate
- tflint --config .tflint.hcl
- aws iam simulate-principal-policy for KMS principal
- Save plan and state snapshot to shared artifact storage and link the ID in the Jira ticket.

End of draft.
